title: Performance profile reconciler and stability watermark exporter
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: onboarding data often contains multiple performance profiles for a single model (variants, quantization levels, hardware affinity). Prior heuristics produced noisy release notes and inconsistent rollouts because we lacked a deterministic reconciliation step and a concise representation of profile stability for changelogs. This PR introduces a profile reconciler that ingests variant-level profiles, normalizes metrics, and synthesizes a single authoritative profile per onboard. It also adds a stability watermark exporter that emits a compact summary used by changelog generation and automated rollout policies.

What this PR does (high level):
- Implements registry/reconciler.py: a deterministic reconciler that merges profiles using configurable weighting (sample counts, recency, occupancy). The reconciler outputs p50/p95 latency, token throughput, GPU occupancy estimates, and a computed stability_score (0-100).
- Adds registry/exporters/watermark.py: formats the reconciled profile into a compact watermark artifact (YAML/JSON) consumed by release note generators and by the rollout controller to determine canary batch sizes. The watermark contains a stability bucket, dominant hardware affinity, and top-line perf deltas vs baseline.
- Adds A/B heuristics: if profiles disagree beyond thresholds (configurable via registry/config.yaml), reconciler emits an alert annotation and includes the high-variance fingerprints in the watermark.
- Changes to changelog pipeline: the changelog assembler now reads watermarks and can inject stability tags and suggested rollout knobs into autogenerated release notes.
- Tests & CI: unit tests for reconciliation math; an e2e integration job (ci/profiles-integration.yml) that validates reconciler + exporter on synthetic variant sets; new fuzz tests to protect against NaNs and missing fields.
- Docs: onboarding/reconciliation.md documents behavior, config knobs, and runbook for resolving high-variance cases.

Key algorithm notes:
- Normalization: metric units are normalized (ms, tokens/sec, percent occupancy).
- Weighting: sample_count and recency (exponential decay) are combined to produce per-variant weights. There is a safeguard floor to avoid starving low-frequency but production-critical variants.
- Stability score: derived from a weighted variance of p95 and occupancy across variants, scaled and clamped to 0-100. This is intentionally conservative (penalizes variance that could cause user-facing regressions).
- Conflict handling: when a variant's p95 delta > delta_threshold and sample_count > min_samples, reconciler annotates the watermark with the variant fingerprint and produces a suggested rollback pointer for the changelog.

Why this is safe: reconciliation is opt-in by default for existing onboard flows; new onboards will run through reconciler but the CR will not flip auto-rollout changes on without the rollout team's explicit opt-in. All exports are signed by the registry service key and stored alongside provenance metadata.

Migration notes: a one-time backfill job (scripts/backfill/reconcile-legacy-profiles.py) is included to generate watermarks for existing models. Backfill is gated behind a feature flag (registry.flags.enable_backfill).

Testing summary: CI runs new unit and integration tests. The integration job spins up a small local registry image, creates synthetic variant profiles (low/high variance), runs reconciliation, and asserts expected watermark fields. Flaky tests were addressed by increasing synthetic dataset entropy and adding deterministic seeds.

Rollout plan: merged to main behind the feature flag. Step 1: run backfill on staging and spot-check 20 high-usage models. Step 2: enable reconciler for new onboards only. Step 3: after 2 weeks of telemetry validation (no spike in rollout aborts), enable reconciliation for all onboards and flip changelog watermark consumption on by default.

Related work: this PR builds on earlier profiling and changelog automation efforts (see ENG-1021 and ENG-1089) and is designed to interoperate with the model registry's provenance fingerprints and release-assembler.

Notes to reviewers: focus on the weighting math in reconciler.py and on the exporter schema stability; small changes to the changelog assembler were intentionally conservative (non-breaking) to avoid regressions in downstream integrations.

Add: stability watermark export used by changelog generation and rollout policies
